subject: Private VPC mesh/gateway demarcation and on-prem handoff — review & action items
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Porter <aporter@edgeops.io>; infra-eng@edgeops.io
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC mesh/gateway demarcation and on-prem handoff — review & action items

Hi Alex / EdgeOps team,

Thanks again for the sync earlier. Attached is v2 of the private-VPC mesh + gateway demarcation diagram and a short deploy runbook. This thread is to capture open items before we finalize the handoff package for your on-prem infra team. High-level goals:

- Clear demarc: control-plane endpoints (certificate authority, control API, rollout service) remain inside the customer subnet with mutually authenticated TLS to Redwood control-plane proxies.
- Data-plane affinity: inference nodes (GPU pods) are placed in a separate tenant VLAN with egress through an EdgeOps gateway cluster we co-manage for peering.
- Minimal L4 ingress: we want only two inbound channels from EdgeOps perimeter to the data-plane (gRPC for runtime, HTTPS for telemetry).

Open questions before we sign-off:
1) NAT vs. routable IPs for inference nodes — you recommended SNAT at the gateway; please confirm support for 1:1 mapping for peer health checks.
2) mTLS termination point — we prefer mTLS end-to-end; confirm whether your gateway can sni-proxy and pass TLS through to edge sidecars.
3) BGP/session failover expectations for multi-rack pods — we outlined a warm-standby plan in the runbook but want your operational play for traffic failover.

Action items proposed:
- EdgeOps to validate port allowlist (gRPC 5100-5110, HTTPS 443, Prometheus 9090) by EOD 6/30.
- Redwood to provide CA CSR + cert rotation cadence and scripts (attached).
- Joint canary plan: 2 racks for 48 hours then incremental roll every 4 racks.

Please reply inline with confirmations or add any additional constraints. If we can get sign-off today we’ll produce the final SOW and a short ATO checklist for your security team.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: soojin_private_vpc_mesh_diag_v2.pdf; redwood_onprem_runbook_v1.md
From: Alex Porter <aporter@edgeops.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-eng@edgeops.io; Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC mesh/gateway demarcation and on-prem handoff — review & action items

Soojin — thanks for the diagram and runbook, good pack. Quick answers inline:

> 1) NAT vs. routable IPs for inference nodes — you recommended SNAT at the gateway; please confirm support for 1:1 mapping for peer health checks.

We can do SNAT and also support 1:1 mapping. 2 caveats: (a) we need a /27 per tenant to guarantee enough ephemeral for burst; (b) health-checking over 1:1 will require static host entries in our probe config (we'll add to the SOW).

> 2) mTLS termination point — we prefer mTLS end-to-end; confirm whether your gateway can sni-proxy and pass TLS through to edge sidecars.

Yes, gateway will SNI-proxy but we can configure passthrough for the runtime ports so mTLS is preserved. Telemetry path is terminated at the gateway for scraping (we'll forward to your scrape endpoint over mutual TLS).

> 3) BGP/session failover expectations for multi-rack pods — we outlined a warm-standby plan in the runbook but want your operational play for traffic failover.

We operate BGP with ECMP and will advertise both primary and secondary prefixes. Failover is sub-30s for session flap; application-level reconnects are typically 10-30s depending on KV cache warm-up. We'll attach our BGP config template.

We validated port allowlist with infra and the range looks fine; we flagged Prometheus port for routing through the management VLAN only.

Next: we'll circulate the edgeops_sow_v3.pdf for legal and confirm /27 allocation by tomorrow. Also will run a quick lab test of TLS passthrough to confirm sidecar cert acceptance.

— Alex
Alex Porter
Edge Infrastructure Lead, EdgeOps Labs
attachments: edgeops_sow_v3.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC mesh/gateway demarcation and on-prem handoff — review & action items

Alex — thanks for the quick confirmation. A few clarifications from Redwood ops side:

- /27 per tenant is acceptable but our preferred CIDR plan expects contiguous allocation for predictable LB hashing. Can you confirm whether allocations can be contiguous or only best-effort?
- For the canary: we need the BGP lab details (AS numbers + nexthop behavior) to script our failover simulation. Please drop those in the Drive link.
- Cert rotation: Soojin, add explicit CSR fields we require (subjectAltNames for runtime FQDNs). We'll also include a KMS integration note for HSM-backed key storage (customer requirement).

I'll attach a short checklist to the Drive folder with the items we need for the security review (syslog endpoint, NTP peering, cert chain, CA fingerprint). If EdgeOps can confirm contiguous allocation and the BGP AS, we can lock the canary window for July 7-9.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Deployments — Redwood Inference

>
> - /27 per tenant is acceptable but our preferred CIDR plan expects contiguous allocation for predictable LB hashing. Can you confirm whether allocations can be contiguous or only best-effort?

Contiguous allocation is possible — we can reserve ranges by tenant and set aside a spare /27 for overflow.

> - For the canary: we need the BGP lab details (AS numbers + nexthop behavior) to script our failover simulation. Please drop those in the Drive link.

We'll add AS 64520 (primary) and 64521 (secondary) along with our EVPN config snippets to the Drive folder by EOD.

> - Cert rotation: Soojin, add explicit CSR fields we require (subjectAltNames for runtime FQDNs). We'll also include a KMS integration note for HSM-backed key storage (customer requirement).

Acknowledged — Lucia (ops) will coordinate with your security team for the CSR and will test the HSM workflow next week.

Action items now:
- EdgeOps: upload BGP/EVPN config + contiguous allocation confirmation (due 2027-07-01).
- Redwood: publish final CSR template + KMS integration note (due 2027-07-01).
- Joint: schedule canary window Jul 7-9 once artifacts are in Drive.

We'll follow with a short readiness call Wed 7/1 at 10:00 PT.

Thanks — Lucia
Lucia Gomez
Operations Manager, EdgeOps Labs
